first: Ha, a new face! I am Pell. I left this valley years ago, but the roads led me back.
I sell a basket, a trowel and some food. And I buy what you find, at a fair price.
A basket opens the grove: herbs and mushrooms. A trowel opens the ruins: you dig for old things. One is enough to start.
stranger: Baskets, trowels, food. And I buy what you find.
A traveller told me there are marks carved into a standing stone down by the river. Old ones.
They say bells ring in the deep ruins at night. Nobody is there to ring them.
acquaintance: Herbs are selling well. The grove has plenty, if you have a basket.
Mushrooms grow thick in the grove to the south. Some of them glow after dark.
There is a glade to the west, past the old oak. The mist sits on it like a lid.
friend: Best customer this side of the river.
The garden behind the ruins was lovely once. Now it is all weeds and whispers.
